=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller package

**Framing:** The Seller's cover note says [STANDARD] clauses are "cleared by both sides" and need no scrutiny, and that the limitation package is "FINAL" and settled at principal level. I can't verify either claim from these documents, and I haven't relied on them. Nearly every item you asked about is marked [STANDARD], and several are the most buyer-adverse terms in the package. I have reviewed all 16 on the merits. The percentages and periods below are suggested opening positions for the deal team to confirm, not agreed terms. Please also check with your principals whether anything was actually settled.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap, with title/capacity and tax at 100% of price and fraud uncapped. Specific indemnities should sit outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at about 30-35% (fall back toward 20-25% only in exchange for a retention or escrow and carve-outs). 20% is acceptable only if the cap applies to the general warranties alone, and the Seller's drafting currently applies it more widely.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis, and an AUD 250,000 deductible basket (about 1% of price) where only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** A lower de minimis, a tipping (first-dollar) basket, and aggregation of related claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a de minimis of about AUD 10,000, a tipping basket of 0.5-1%, and related claims aggregated. A deductible basket on a 24m deal gives the Seller a free AUD 250k, and the de minimis could strip out many small SaaS-type claims.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion, and any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months for general warranties, so the period covers two audit cycles. Longer periods apply to tax, title and fundamental matters, and the "applies to all Claims" language is deleted.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and reject the blanket sentence, because it would override the longer periods for the other categories.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Title and capacity capped at 100% of price (or total consideration received), outside the basket and de minimis, with a long claim period (at least 6 years).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Failure of title defeats the whole purchase, and a 4.8m cap on a 24m asset does not protect the Buyer.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** None in the package. Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature", which on its face captures fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out. No cap, basket, time limit, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause limits liability for fraud, dishonest concealment or wilful misconduct, including by the Company's management before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on it. It is a must-have, and the Seller's current drafting is unacceptable.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, with sufficient detail to identify the matter and its nature. No general disclosure of the data room or public registers, and no disclosure against title, capacity or tax. Later disclosures must not cure breaches.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. It would let the Seller neutralise most warranties by pointing to a document in the data room.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** No knowledge-based exclusion. The Buyer's rights should be expressly unaffected by its knowledge or investigations (a pro-sandbagging clause). If a concession is needed, limit it to the actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals of a specifically disclosed matter.
- **Recommendation:** Delete clause 8.3. "Discoverable" is constructive knowledge and, combined with general disclosure, would largely remove the warranty protection.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours", with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of any written consent. The Disclosure Letter admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** A condition precedent requiring unconditional consent, or consent on terms the Buyer approves, with the clause 11.3 conditions satisfied. It should be waivable by the Buyer only, with no termination or renegotiation right and a long-stop date.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's wording. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or about 30% of revenue, so the deal should not close without it. If the Buyer waives the condition, use a price adjustment or retention.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release to be provided *after* Completion. About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and unrepaid, and no discharge has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion from the price, using a payout letter and a funds-flow line, with simultaneous release of the security and PPSR discharge. This follows from the debt-free/cash-free basis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with secured debt, and the change-control clause 8.1 may also be triggered.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses and on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) treated as transaction costs or debt-like items, deducted from the price or paid through the funds flow and payroll.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Company owes these amounts, so they fall on the Buyer unless deducted. Ask the Seller to quantify the on-costs, which the Disclosure Letter does not.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** Evidence of cleared payment, plus a confirmatory IP assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials as a condition. The indemnity should cover loss from any failure of IP ownership or transfer, sit outside the cap and basket, and be backed by a retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted. DD-004 clause 7.3 ties the IP transfer to payment of *every* SOW3 fee, and AUD 180,000 is shown as open. The risk is loss of IP, not just the AUD 180k, and the Disclosure Letter says there is no payment receipt or assignment.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity for all losses from the incident (regulatory, notification, remediation, third-party claims), with no cap or basket. Also a covenant to investigate, assess and notify as required, with Buyer information and consultation rights before Completion, and possibly a retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation. The Seller's own letter says about 1,240 personal records may be affected, and that access, scope and notification are unknown. Take advice on whether the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)) assessment has been done. The Seller's disclosure is dated 22 September, so the 30-day assessment period may already have run.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs (AUD 330,000 across three renewals of AUD 110,000).
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure of the commitment terms (committed or terminable, prepaid or accrued, timing and scope). Treat committed or accrued amounts as debt-like items or working-capital adjustments if they are not ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** Hold the position and request information. The Disclosure Letter does not support "ordinary course" and says the renewals should be read together, which suggests they are one related commitment.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** One regime for everything: "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise", with the limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses applying to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud, each with its own cap, thresholds and time limits.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The blanket clause is the mechanism that undermines most of the other protections, so fix the structure first.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. The Seller concedes this is not Buyer-verified.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification (ASIC extract, share issue and transfer history, constitution and shareholder agreements). Also confirmation that the shares are free of encumbrances, including any Riverlark security, and a title warranty and deliverables at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the register as proof. Complete verification as a condition and see SPA-N-004 for the warranty.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** A tax indemnity and tax warranties with a claim period matching the tax amendment period, which I haven't verified for this entity (typically up to about 4-5 years). Core IP ownership warranties should have a higher cap and a longer period than the general warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as open and reject "settled". Nothing in the package shows these terms were negotiated.

---

**Other points**
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says neither document requires consent for a share sale. I have not seen the underlying documents. Have them checked for change-of-control language and add warranties.
- **Disclosure Letter 1.4:** The non-admission language is acceptable only if it doesn't undercut the warranties or indemnities.
- **Priorities:** The five most important points are the fraud carve-out, the Riverlark payout at Completion, deletion of the buyer-knowledge clause, rejecting general disclosure, and separating the liability categories.

I can turn these into a mark-up of the SPA clauses or a short issues list for the principals, if useful.
